hardware: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S (laptop; power- and thermal-limited, gross numbers). Clock-sensitive rows are provisional pending re-measurement on the desktop gfx1151 host.
change: gguf_iq_dense_strict_kernel gains an R rows-per-block tile alongside its T=8 column tile. Each decoded weight is reused across R prompt-row activations instead of being re-decoded once per row. Before this change the dense IQ 'prefill_*' and 'gemv_*' registry variants resolved to the same launcher with grid.y = rows, so weight bytes were re-read once per prompt row. R only changes which rows share a workgroup: per-(row, column) k ownership, FMA order, wave32 shuffle tree and serial wave-0..3 sum are unchanged, so every R is bit-identical to R=1 and the change is strict, not production-profile.
method: Same-session A/B. All arms run in one process against one resident model or one device weight buffer, alternating, so they share clock and thermal state; min-of-N (kernel) and max-of-N (end-to-end) are reported. Sequential single-variant runs were rejected as a protocol: two runs of byte-identical machine code differed by 10% on this host.
noise_floor: +/-5%, established in the same interleaved table by quants whose ISA is unchanged across arms (IQ3_S, Q3_K).

row_slab_sweep.protocol: scratchpad/rowbatch_bench.py, largest rank-2 tensor per family from Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_S, f32 out, explicit row_batch, min-of-5 rounds
row_slab_sweep.note: ms per launch; speedup is R=1 (previous behaviour) over the best slab
row_slab_sweep.rows_1: R=1 remains fastest at rows=1 for every family (IQ4_XS 0.552 ms vs 1.039 ms at R=8), which is what the shipped default selects; decode is unaffected.

e2e_gross.protocol: scratchpad/ud_e2e_ab.py; Qwen35GGUFResidentSession, 97-token prompt, bulk prefill, 63 decode steps, greedy; arms alternated in one resident session; best of 2 rounds after a warm round for each arm
e2e_gross.note: Decode is identical by construction: the default selects R=1 at rows=1. These absolute rates use a different harness from the 2026-09-08 raw-Q5/Q6 row (5.52/6.39 tok/s) and are not comparable to it; only the within-session ratio is claimed.

R16_rejected.reason: hits the VGPR cap and spills; R=8 is the retained maximum

resource_usage.note: R=1 codegen is unchanged from before this commit (43 VGPRs, 16 waves/SIMD), so the decode path is untouched.

profiling.tool: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace, prebuilt .so with HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 and an explicit compiler-version file
profiling.confirms: gguf_iq_dense_strict_kernel<0, true, 8, 8> is the production prefill route (117 calls, 1748.57 ms); Q=1/2/3 instantiations also run at R=8
profiling.prefill_share: raw IQ dense fell from 50.2% of prefill device time to 25.2%; gguf_k_prefill_out_rowbatch_kernel<*,*,5,32> (raw Q5_K) is now the largest prefill consumer at 41.5%

host_side.change: gguf_iq_dense.launch() memoizes the loaded CDLL. It previously called build_gguf_iq_dense() on every invocation when no library was passed, which re-reads and SHA-256s the kernel sources to recompute the build cache key.
host_side.note: Paid once per projection per layer on the hot path. No separate throughput claim is made for this; it is included in the end-to-end rows above.

correctness.row_slab_parity: tests/test_gguf_ud_dense_rowbatch.py 195/195 - every R in (2,4,8) bit-identical to R=1 across all seven quants, both output dtypes, and 13 row counts including ragged tails (3,5,7,9,15,17,33); output canaries assert padding rows never store
correctness.exact_parity: tests/test_gguf_ud_dense.py 84/84 bit-exact vs the 128-strided-accumulator reference plus its CPU outer KL/top-1 gate, with the new default slab selection active
correctness.suites: test_gguf_ud_admission.py, test_qwen35_gguf_consumer_surface_parity.py, test_gfx1151_backend.py, test_gguf_iq_dense_tables_closed_form.py, test_gguf_e2e_acceptance.py, test_gguf_ud_km.py, test_gguf_ud_ks.py all green

limitations: Laptop power/clock limited: absolute rates are gross and provisional; the desktop gfx1151 host is the confirmation target.
The row tile helps prefill only. Decode (rows=1) is unchanged by construction and remains the open target.

tests/test_qwen35_gguf_iq_dispatch.py fails to collect on a pre-existing circular import in hipengine/generation/registry.py, reproduced at HEAD with these changes reverted; unrelated to this unit and not addressed here.

revisit_on_desktop_gfx1151.why: Every wall-clock row here comes from a power- and thermal-limited laptop with a measured +/-5% floor. Direction is safe where ISA or a >3x ratio backs it; magnitude is not. Re-measurement is cheap once a desktop gfx1151 is free.
confident_direction_uncertain_magnitude: Row-slab speedups (2.97-4.05x kernel, 1.73x end-to-end prefill) are far outside the noise floor, so the win is real; the exact ratios are not final.

R=8 over R=4 is only 10-13% at rows>=128 and ~10% at rows=8. R=8 costs occupancy (10 vs 16 waves/SIMD). The crossover may move on a host with different clock behaviour - re-sweep before treating R=8 as final.
inconclusive_here: B2/B5 sign and magnitude arithmetic: retained on instruction-count evidence (loads 50->34 on IQ3_XXS and IQ2_XS). Wall clock read +4.9% (IQ2_XS) and +1.1% (IQ3_XXS), both inside the floor. Confirm sign and size.

B1 IQ4 codebook immediates rejected at -5.0%, which is exactly the floor. The +112 VALU in the ISA supports the direction and the VALU-bound model, but one confirmation pass would settle it. If the desktop shows it neutral-or-positive, the VALU-bound model for this kernel needs revisiting.

The end-to-end harness used here reports decode 4.23 tok/s where the 2026-09-08 raw-Q5/Q6 row reports 6.39 from a different harness. Protocols should be reconciled so future UD rows are comparable rather than only self-consistent.
not_yet_swept: T x R jointly. T=8 was tuned at R=1; the best column tile may differ once R=8 consumes registers for row accumulators.
Per-role slab selection. The shipped policy is one global function of rows; the raw-K family instead qualifies specific (quant, output, K, N) shapes. Whether IQ needs that is unmeasured.
R=8 at rows between 2 and 8, where the slab is partly padding.
queue_not_started: B3 LDS grid staging - the remaining global_load_u8 mass (IQ3_S 64, IQ3_XXS/IQ2_S 48 per body) is grid-table lookups; LDS use is only 2176-3200 B/block against 64 KB. Note the B1 lesson: this only pays if it does not add VALU.
B4 payload dword loads - authorized as a production-profile variant this phase.
A5 dense entry point over the existing selected-shape IQ integer-MMQ prefill kernels.

A6 host trace: the ~12 s host vs ~1.2 s GPU dense-era figure has not been re-measured since the row tile landed, and prefill is now 1.73x faster on the device side, so the host share is proportionally larger.
Decode (rows=1) is untouched by this unit and remains the open target: IQ2_XS 41-45 GB/s against Q5_K/Q6_K at 125-147 GB/s on the same host.
